title: What to Watch This Week: Sherlock's Kidnapped, the Silos Are Cracking, and the X-Men Are Lost in Time
excerpt: From Enola Holmes 3 on Netflix to Silo's 100% Rotten Tomatoes comeback on Apple TV+, here are 7 streaming picks worth your time this week.
body:
The first week of July is stacked. Whether you're a sci-fi purist, a Bollywood loyalist, or someone who's still not over Meryl Streep in glasses, your streaming queue just got seriously long. Here are the seven picks actually worth pressing play on.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=BLBvbMtjyAQ

---

1. Enola Holmes 3 — Netflix (July 1)

Millie Bobby Brown is back as the youngest Holmes sibling, and this time it's personal. Literally — Sherlock has been kidnapped, and Enola has to rescue him while also planning her wedding in Malta. Henry Cavill and Louis Partridge return, and the franchise's signature mix of wit, Victorian costuming, and surprisingly decent fight choreography is intact. Available in English, Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu.

*Our take: Comfort viewing, perfectly executed. Not revolutionary, but genuinely fun — and the Malta location work is gorgeous.*

---

2. X-Men '97 Season 2 — JioHotstar (July 1)

The animated series that made grown adults cry over Saturday morning cartoons is back. After that devastating Season 1 finale, the X-Men are scattered across time — Professor X and Magneto stranded in Ancient Egypt (3000 BC), Cyclops and Jean Grey flung into 3960 AD, and Bishop desperately trying to pull them all back together. Nine episodes. One Omega-level nemesis. Zero chill.

*Our take: If you haven't watched Season 1 yet, clear your evening. You have approximately zero excuses.*

---

> "Critics are calling the final two episodes "mind-blowing." CBR gave it a perfect 10/10."

3. Elle: From the World of Legally Blonde — Prime Video (July 1)

Before she conquered Harvard, there was high school. This prequel series follows a teenage Elle Woods (played by newcomer Lexi Minetree) navigating the pink-tinted chaos of her formative years. It's lighter fare, but the *Legally Blonde* franchise has always understood something most comedies forget: you can be bubbly and brilliant at the same time. Available in English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam.

*Our take: Worth trying if you loved the originals. Don't expect depth — expect vibes.*

---

4. Super Subbu — Netflix (July 2)

![Meryl Streep — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/Meryl_Streep-_Press_conference_for_the_film_%22The_Devil_Wears_Prada_2%22_-_55194765350_%28cropped1%29.jpg)

Netflix's first original Telugu series, and the concept practically writes itself. Sundeep Kishan plays a sheltered young man whose conservative father (the brilliant Murali Sharma) never wanted him near anything remotely romantic. Naturally, he ends up teaching sex education to adults in a rural village. Mithila Palkar co-stars. Eight episodes of pure comedic chaos, available in Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, and Hindi.

*Our take: This has sleeper hit written all over it. The trailer is already viral in Telugu circuits, and the cast is stacked.*

---

5. Silo Season 3 — Apple TV+ (July 3) ⭐ PICK OF THE WEEK

The one you absolutely cannot miss. Rebecca Ferguson's underground dystopia is back with a 100% Rotten Tomatoes score — matching its stellar first season and decisively improving on a divisive second. This time, the show splits between Juliette's present-day resistance inside the silo and a stunning new "Before Times" timeline featuring Ashley Zukerman as a US congressman and Jessica Henwick as an investigative journalist, unravelling how the world ended.

Critics are calling the final two episodes "mind-blowing." CBR gave it a perfect 10/10. Radio Times says the finale is "the best episode of the whole show." Weekly releases through September 4.

*Our take: The best sci-fi show on any platform right now. Period. If you've never watched Silo, start from Season 1 — you'll thank us later.*

---

6. Pritam and Pedro — JioHotstar (July 3)

Rajkumar Hirani — the man behind *3 Idiots*, *PK*, and *Munna Bhai* — makes his OTT debut with this buddy-cop series pairing Arshad Warsi as a seasoned old-school detective with Vir Hirani (yes, the director's son, who played young Circuit at age six in *Lage Raho Munna Bhai*) as a tech-obsessed newbie. Sanjay Dutt and Boman Irani show up for cameos that reportedly had the entire set in tears. It's Hirani doing what Hirani does best: warmth, comedy, and just enough heart to catch you completely off guard.

*Our take: If Hirani's name is on it, you watch. Simple as that.*

---

7. Muthassi — ZEE5 (July 3)

For horror fans who like their scares steeped in mythology. This Malayalam series follows a mother who returns to her ancestral Tulu village along the Kerala-Karnataka border, where an ancient demonic entity possesses her young son. Saniya Iyappan and Anarkali Marikar lead a cast that navigates seven episodes of blood rituals, dark family secrets, and the kind of atmospheric dread that South Indian horror does better than anyone.

*Our take: Regional horror continues to be India's most underrated genre. If you've been sleeping on Malayalam content, this is your wake-up call.*
